### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via newPassword (literal, a string literal in runAdminSetUserPassword))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8bc6ea0d22863c031aa637070414dd7849a48180` — the merge of head `ab706f70612cd6e99a4ca9a4e88a51b9a9cc33bb` into base `2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8bc6ea0d22863c031aa637070414dd7849a48180 && git checkout 8bc6ea0d22863c031aa637070414dd7849a48180
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 ab706f70612cd6e99a4ca9a4e88a51b9a9cc33bb && git checkout -B drift-repro 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 && git merge --no-ff ab706f70612cd6e99a4ca9a4e88a51b9a9cc33bb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d151a9871caadca99f254b6766aa475848a6e5ba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.test.ts + .changeset/25824-admin-create-user-password-length.md, better-auth 1.7.12 dist/plugins/admin/routes.mjs, better-auth 1.7.12 dist/utils/password.mjs, better-auth 1.7.12 dist/context/create-context.mjs, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, docs/adr/0069-enterprise-authentication-hardening.md, content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx

Face: `narrowing` (the PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; no governed path, no published schema in the file list). Inputs: card #25824 body and all six comments (triage 6401086406, claims 6407745341 / 6407761859, withdrawal 6407776655, arbitration 6407784753, os-dev-report 6408177252), PR #25927 body, file list (3 files: +192 / -33) and the net diff against `main` at the head, and the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run; the dev's test counts and ablation readings are reported as the dev's, not re-measured.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, with the cited code it was read against.

1. **create-user refuses an explicit `password` shorter than `minPasswordLength`** with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` "Password must be at least N characters" — RIGHT. The card's repro (`password: 'a'` answered 200 and signed in) is the defect; better-auth 1.7.12 `admin/create-user` runs only `assertPasswordNotTooLong` (routes.mjs line 194) while `admin/set-user-password` runs both assertions (lines 828-829), so the hunks' premise holds in the installed version. The range is read from `getAuthContext().password.config`, which better-auth resolves as `minPasswordLength || 8` / `maxPasswordLength || 128` (create-context.mjs lines 185-188) from `emailAndPassword.*`, the field `auth-plugin.ts` maps `password_min_length` / `password_max_length` onto (lines 2013-2019, through `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` lines 375-378) — the ADR-0069 row the body cites. One accept set shrinks; this is the narrowing the Clause line declares.
2. **The refusal lands before anything is written** — RIGHT. `runAdminCreateUser` reads the context and resolves the password before the multi-org join, the permission-set grant, `createUser`, the must-change stamp and the audit row. The new pins assert no `createUser`, no hash, no account write, no engine update and no audit insert on each refusal.
3. **create-user's too-long refusal changes code**: before, a password over `maxPasswordLength` was refused by better-auth and mapped by `mapAuthApiError` as `400 PASSWORD_TOO_LONG`; now it is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` "Password must be at most N characters" — RIGHT per the triage route (6401086406: "with the same code" as set-user-password), and disclosed on the Clause line in both carriers. Note for the seat: the BREAKING banner's Before / Now bullets name only the short-password case; a client matching `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG` on this one door sees the changed code without a banner line for it. No error-code ledger or doc ties `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG` to the admin door (grep over spec, ADRs, scripts and docs: no hit), so nothing else is falsified. Non-blocking.
4. **set-user-password's explicit-password accept set is unchanged** — RIGHT. Its own length check (the deleted lines 1035-1041 on `main`) is reproduced verbatim inside `resolvePassword`; the check order stays userId, then required / complexity, then length. The one observable difference is that an unreadable auth context now refuses before "newPassword is required" and before the complexity check, through the same `mapAuthApiError(error, 'set-user-password failed')` it already used. Right, and stated in the PR body.
5. **A generated password is sized `min(max(16, minPasswordLength), maxPasswordLength)` on both doors** — RIGHT, and it closes the latent set-user-password self-refusal above a 16 minimum. The range check runs on the generated value too. Edge, non-blocking: with `maxPasswordLength` below 12 the generator's floor of 12 still applies and the request answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST` "Password must be at most N characters" to a client that asked for generation; the manifest's floor for `password_max_length` is 16, so this is reachable only through a construction-time config, never through the settings door.
6. **create-user gains a failure mode when the auth context cannot be read**: `mapAuthApiError(error, 'create-user failed')`, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` on a plain Error, no account — RIGHT. In that state `createUser` could not have run either; the pin covers it. Production wiring supplies `getAuthContext` through the shared `adminUserDeps()` factory in `auth-plugin.ts` (line 3240), the same factory both runners already read.
7. **Public surface** — RIGHT, unchanged. `admin-user-endpoints.ts` is on the package barrel (`index.ts` line 52, `export *`), so its exports are the package's: `generateTemporaryPassword(length = 16)` keeps its signature and 12-floor, `AuthContextLike`, `AdminUserEndpointDeps` (`getAuthContext` was already required), `runAdminCreateUser`, `runAdminSetUserPassword`, `mapAuthApiError`, `isLikelyEmail`, `normalizePhoneNumber` are byte-unchanged in signature. `resolvePassword`, `temporaryPasswordLength` and `PasswordLengthPolicy` are module-private. The library-side face of the narrowing is behavioural only: a host whose `getAuthContext` throws now gets a 500 from create-user instead of an account.
8. **Metadata-protocol: none** — RIGHT. No spec key, authorable value, object definition or stored shape moves; the sys_user `create_user` / `set_user_password` dialog actions (pinned in the "Setup dialogs" describe) are untouched and still send `generatePassword: true` as a constant with explicit-wins.
9. **Pre-existing, not this PR's, named so the seat has it**: the manifest allows `password_min_length` up to 64 and `password_max_length` down to 16 with no cross-field check, so an inverted range (min 64, max 16) refuses every password on both admin doors and on better-auth's own sign-up. The diff neither introduces nor worsens it.

The new describe block (17 pins: per door, from one table, three refusals, two boundaries, one configured range and two generated sizes, plus create-user's unreadable-context pin) reads correctly against the mock's default range 8 / 128: 'Abcde1!' is 7, 'Abcdef1!' is 8, the maximum pins are 128 and 129 characters. The pre-existing "enforces better-auth min password length" pin on set-user-password is kept and, per the dev's ablation A, goes red when the shared check is deleted.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth`: **patch**, with the BREAKING banner, Before / Now / Fix, both declaration lines and one ADR-0087 marker — RIGHT per the Post-Task Checklist step 3: a non-protocol change, breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on the PR body and in the changeset body, the arm word first inside the parenthesis, so `clause2-line.mjs` reads it; `Metadata-protocol: none` on both. Disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the changeset's Fix is a request edit (send a password inside the range, or `generatePassword: true`), not a consumer-code rewrite, and no exported declaration is removed or narrowed (judgment 7), so the category's own precondition holds; `Check Changeset` (the lane that runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) is green on this head. The only package the diff moves is the one the changeset bumps. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong and is not used. The PR title's `fix(plugin-auth)!:` matches the banner.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev's report (6408177252) and the PR's Acceptance notes, each answered:

- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- **out_of_scope_findings 1 / Acceptance note 1 — admin import-users is not sized to the range.** Confirmed by reading: `admin-import-users.ts` line 690 calls `generateTemporaryPassword()` with no length, its deps carry no `getAuthContext`, and better-auth's `createUser` checks only the maximum, so on a deployment with `password_min_length` above 16 (the manifest allows up to 64) `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/import-users` with `passwordPolicy: 'temporary'` or an `auto` fallback saves 16-character credentials below the minimum. Import rows carry no explicit password, so the short-explicit face does not reach that door. This is the card's defect class on a sibling door and is reachable by an administrator over public HTTP; the dev noted it without filing because reach was read, not measured live. **Escalated to the seat: file it as its own card** (dedupe words: "import-users temporary password minPasswordLength", "generateTemporaryPassword length import"). Outside this claim's file surface; it does not hold this PR.
- **out_of_scope_findings 2 / Acceptance note 2 — two codes for one policy** (`INVALID_REQUEST` on the admin doors, `PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT` / `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG` on better-auth's sign-up and change-password). Accepted: the triage route asked for set-user-password's code, and aligning the admin doors to better-auth's codes would change set-user-password's existing wire answer. Judgment 3 names the one code that did move.
- **Acceptance note 3 — complexity before length.** Accepted: the order is set-user-password's prior order; `password_require_complexity` is off by default, which is why the card's one-character password reached `createUser` at all.
- **Gates NOT MEASURED locally.** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is hosted by `Build Core` (success on this head); `check:type-check-debt` is `Type Check · debt ledger` (success).
- **Claim race.** Resolved on the card: seat 1 withdrew (6407776655), the seat arbitrated to 6407745341 (6407784753), and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` is green.
- **Docs drift bot** flagged `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` via `newPassword`. Read: the admin create-user / set-user-password section states no length rule and the ADR-0069 settings table lists no length row, so nothing on that page is falsified; no doc edit is owed by this PR.
- **Ablations** (BASE 9 / 84, A 9 / 84, B 4 / 89) and the dogfood battery (296 files, 2523 passed) are the dev's readings on `d151a987`; not re-run here, consistent with the pins as read.

**Check-runs on `d151a987` at the time of this record (2026-10-26T04:31Z)**: 31 success (among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, every Lint lane, Type Check consumer / source / debt ledger / workspace, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core 2/8, 6/8, 7/8, 8/8), 10 skipped by path selection (UI, docs, Temporal, opt-in harnesses), 4 still in progress (Test Core 1/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8). No failure. The verdict below stands on the diff and the completed gates; the seat reads the four shards to green before the queue.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8sle7x`
Reviewed-by: `session_01TFnDdepdwyDJeM2kJ4GtMy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
